instances.fault_description: The multi-character path of Metaphone.metaphone uppercases with Locale.getDefault() instead of Locale.ENGLISH. Under tr_TR, 'i' becomes dotted capital 'İ', which is outside the front-vowel set, so the C in 'cider' takes the hard branch and isMetaphoneEqual('cider','sider') returns false.
instances.local_cue_gold_note: An explicit Locale.getDefault() sits next to a single-character branch that uses Locale.ENGLISH. It is the only Locale.getDefault in the package, and the test visibly sets the tr_TR default.
instances.notes: Nominally L50 (50 claimed units), but there is no attribution ambiguity: a single grep for locale use finds the fault. stage-report/negative_results.csv cites this as an example that chain length is not hypothesis-selection difficulty.

instances.fault_description: The single-character read() now increments lineCounter for CR only when the previous char is not LF, so an LF-CR pair counts as one terminator. The parser's records stay correct, but getLineNumber reports 3 instead of 5.
instances.local_cue_gold_note: The symmetric CR/LF suppression condition differs from the bulk read(char[],int,int) overload in the same class, which counts LF-CR as two breaks (the agent cited this).
instances.notes: Hops: getRecords -> getRecord -> CSVLexer.nextToken -> ExtendedBufferedReader.read. The count is reported through a separate getter chain (parser -> lexer -> reader getLineNumber), which is a state-propagation path. Both read overloads score as gold by name. The variant report concedes that the public line-number assertion narrows the subsystem.

instances.fault_description: Partial(types, values, chronology) checks largest-smallest order only through DurationField.compareTo and never special-cases unsupported duration fields such as eras. UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo returns 1 against supported fields, and BaseDurationField compares unit millis against 0, so [year, era, monthOfYear] is accepted instead of rejected with IllegalArgumentException.
instances.local_cue_gold_note: UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo's Javadoc says 'Always returns zero', but the code returns 1. Partial.with has isSupported checks that the constructor lacks.
instances.local_cue_decoy_note: BaseDurationField.compareTo is correct but yields an asymmetric positive result against 0-millis unsupported fields. It was ranked 2nd, above the gold UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo (4th).
instances.notes: Ownership is split between the comparator definer (UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo) and its consumer (the Partial constructor), and both count as gold, so the split did not hurt the score. Dynamic dispatch on compareTo depends on which side is unsupported (year.compareTo(eras) runs BaseDurationField; eras.compareTo(months) runs UnsupportedDurationField). Partial.with acts as a second caller that handles unsupported fields explicitly. The agent's evidence chain names both repair options ('explicit handling in Partial ordering, or corrected comparison semantics').

instances.fault_description: CategoryPlot.getRenderer(int) remaps every positive renderer index to slot 0. instances.local_cue_decoy_note: The competitors (getLegendItems loop, getIndexOf reverse lookup, renderer getLegendItems) are unmodified and read as idiomatic.

Its depth was audited at 12 units, not the nominal 25 (depth-reaudit-2026-09-14.md). chart-1-dependency-audit.md section 6 notes that a solver can rank getRenderer after inspecting only CategoryPlot.getLegendItems. The agent ranked the gold first and put getLegendItems/getIndexOf at 2 and 5. getRenderer is also used by other plot operations (the variant report's limitations section), so it has callers beyond the trigger.

The gate falls through and CallSiteOptimizer strips the callback's unused trailing formal and the matching call argument, which breaks the observed Function.prototype.length.

That valid trailing-parameter fallback looks like a bypass of canChangeSignature, and the agent's evidence chain cited exactly this as the root cause.

instances.instance_label: Csv-1 original Defects4J (1 run, gold rank 1)
instances.fault_description: ExtendedBufferedReader.read() increments lineCounter only for '\n'. It omits counting a standalone '\r' (and the CRLF de-duplication via lastChar), so parsing "a\rb\rc" with CR as the line separator leaves getLineNumber() at 0 instead of 1.
instances.local_cue_gold_note: The sibling overload read(char[],int,int) in the same class explicitly counts both standalone CR and CRLF, while read() counts only LF. The agent used this contrast.
instances.local_cue_decoy_note: Lexer.isEndOfLine correctly treats CR as EOL. The getLineNumber delegation chain is trivial.
instances.notes: The chain is getRecord -> CSVLexer.nextToken (and simpleTokenLexer) -> in.read(). The observed counter is read back through CSVParser.getLineNumber -> Lexer.getLineNumber -> ExtendedBufferedReader.getLineNumber, which is state propagation. Why CLOSURE-1-NAME-L10-001 failed (from its submission and tool calls):
- The agent read the gold guard and saw that it contradicts the comment above it.
- It still put CallSiteOptimizer.markUnreferencedFunctionArgs first. That method is in the same file, its name matches the symptom ('unreferenced function args'), and its correct rule ('|| !hasFollowing', remove the last formal) directly explains the .length removal.
- This fits the reports' salience and ownership account: the downstream executor wins on local and lexical evidence (M11, M12, M6, M20), while the pass-config evidence that points to the guard is about 9 hops away (M19).

Why the 8 correct cases were easy: each had a strong local cue in the gold line itself (Locale.getDefault(), p1 vs maxDenominator, instanceof Class, the stale sentinel, the long-first scan, the missing guard under its own comment), and usually a sibling oracle in the repo (Metaphone's Locale.ENGLISH, BigFraction's q1, Options.getOption's short-first rule, the bulk read(char[]) overload, Partial.with). Competitors were mostly stack-top or delegating methods: createInteger, getActualType, getOptionValues. Even where a correct competitor looked locally odd (UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo always returning 0, getActualType's do/while), the gold kept rank 1 when its own cue was strong and no lexical decoy beat it.

Caveats:
- Each variant here has one run, and the reports document run-to-run variance on the Closure cells.
